column1: # skip-ledger.tsv — what may skip, one line per reason.
# REPLACES the single-number-per-job budget. That file took 37 commits in three
# days and held one line of 120,780 characters, because three streams edited the
# SAME NUMBER and resolved additively; ten of those resolutions were on one line
# in two days, and three had EQUAL NUMBERS ON BOTH SIDES -- 596 vs 596, which
# were not the same 596. Equal numbers on both sides of a conflict do not look
# like a conflict, which is why that shape had to go rather than be managed.
# FORMAT, tab-separated:
#   <job key>
column4: <why it may skip>

column1: # A job's budget is the SUM of its lines. Adding a skipping test means adding a
# NEW LINE, which is why two streams doing it at once no longer conflict: git
# merges distinct lines. Nobody edits a total, because there is no total.
# EACH LINE IS CHECKED INDIVIDUALLY. The regex must match exactly <count> skips
# in the run. A line matching fewer is stale -- the test stopped skipping, or was
# renamed -- and fails. A line matching more means something new is skipping
# under a reason written for something else.
# THE __UNATTRIBUTED__ LINE IS A RATCHET. It carries the skips inherited from the
# old single-number budget, which were never attributed to reasons. It may only
# SHRINK. A new skip that matches no pattern lands here, pushes the count over,
# and fails -- so a new skip must be attributed by name. That is the forcing
# function: the legacy remainder cannot grow, only be worked down.
# WHAT A SKIP COSTS, which has been got wrong four times:
#   * a test running against registeredBackends costs TWO skips (its mysql and
#     mssql arms) in every PostgreSQL-only job -- test-go/engine AND cluster,
#     which move together;
#   * a test gated on CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL / CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL costs ONE in whichever
#     job runs its package without that dialect;
#   * a toolchain-gated test costs ONE in every job that does not install it.
# Attribute by NAME, never by delta: run the new test with
#   go test ./<pkg>/ -run <Name> -json | grep '"Action":"skip"'
# and count what it actually reports.
# A skip is indistinguishable from a pass. Where a job PROVISIONS a resource the
# right number is 0: a skip there means something it set up did not arrive.

column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: the test runs one subtest per dialect and each calls testutil.TestDB, which skips when that dialect's DSN is unset. Both of these jobs supply PostgreSQL only, so mysql and mssql skip and postgres RUNS -- two, not three, and not the one a single-gate test costs. Measured by name, not by delta: go test ./engine/ -run TestTheDatabaseHasTheLatestDefinitionOfEveryRoutineTheMigrationsShip -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' -- with no DSN at all it is 3, with CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES set it is 2.
